title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Starting point
AI system and date: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Monday, November 9th.
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.

Core model: ARR_DELAY_NEW ~ DAY_OF_WEEK (7 levels) + DISTANCE (miles) + TAXI_IN (minutes) + TAXI_OUT (minutes) + DEP_DELAY_NEW (minutes) + OP_UNIQUE_CARRIER (13 levels)


Question: How do a variety of factors (like the ones above) impact the Arrival delays of flights?


Baseline result: Our model had an R² of approximately 0.98, meaning it explained about 98% of the variation in arrival delays. Compared to Monday (our baseline day), only Saturday and Sunday did not have statistically significant effects. All other coefficients were statistically significant.


We still hope to work on coding up hubs into our data, as well as determining which predictors can help us actually make actual predictions, rather than just being able to fit the model (i.e. we don’t want to overfit).

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Substantive prompts
Paste the exact prompts that shaped the extension. Include the customized extension-selection prompt from the checkpoint and any important implementation follow-ups. Delete unused prompt blocks.

I am creating a regression case study in R and Quarto. My question is “what factors impact flight delays”. The response is the minutes of arrival delay, the main predictors are found in the proposal template that’s attached, as is the model. My main result so far is that pretty much everything is significant. I found this limitation or opportunity: We can’t predict very well, because our predictors rely on information known after a flight lands. Suggest three feasible extensions that keep the core analysis connected to regression methods taught in my class. One option may be a model not taught in class used as a comparator. For each, explain how it strengthens the same research question, how its result would enter the final case study, the implementation steps, and two ways I could verify it. Do not choose for me.

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
My decisions

Accepted: What useful advice did you use? > Claude suggested using a timing ladder, where we fit different models based on what information is available at different times to see how well we can predict flight delays at different points. Additionally, we are going to use random forest model as a comparator model, to see how well our linear models actually do at predicting (in addition to CV). The random forest model is the AI extension.
Changed: What did you adapt to fit your data or goals? > We are not going to run lasso regression, because we want to see the effects for every day of the week and across each airline. If we remove any airlines or days, then this model isn’t generalizable.
Rejected or corrected: What advice was unsuitable, unnecessary, or wrong? > Discussions about looking at standard errors instead of p-values was something that we were not interested in doing and it was unsuitable forus.

Connection to the final case study: Identify where the extension’s method and result appear on the final page and how they strengthen the course-based analysis.

We are going to use a random forest method with each of our timing slots to compare it to our LM CV RMSE to see if our LM model is actually good at predicting things. The results will appear right next to any LM results to provide the comparison point.
